Part of https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1180 implementation. ~Depends on #40999~ #### TODO: - TextServer interface. ✔️ - TextServer Fallback implementation (based on existing Font implementations) ✔️ - Dynamic font data ✔️ - Bitmap font data ✔️ - TextServer ICU + HarfBuzz implementation. ✔️ - Dynamic font data ✔️ - Bitmap font data ✔️ - TextServer documentation ✔️ - TextServer unit test + test project ✔️ - Font class refactoring ✔️ - Simple controls (everything except `Label`, `LineEdit`, `TextEdit`, `RichTextLabel`) TS base text ✔️ - Interface mirroring ✔️ - Add BiDi override for path `LineEdit`s and `CodeEdit` ✔️ - Complex controls ✔️ - `Label` ✔️ - `LineEdit` ✔️ - `TextEdit` + `CodeEdit` ✔️ - `RichTextLabel` (probably will be done as the separate PR) - Editor tools for Font substitution config and TS data export ✔️ - Update controls / font documentation ✔️ - Bump `MessageQuery` size to 2048 KB to handle additional `LineEdit` / `TextEdit` popup submenus (superseded by #42296) ✔️ #### Breaking changes: - `BitmapFont`, `DynamicFont` and `DyamicFontData` are removed and replaced with universal `Font` + `FontData`, actual implementation is handled by `TextServer`. - Font size and outline parameters are no longer font properties and can be passed to draw functions directly, theme properties added accordingly. - `Font` and `CanvasItem` API changes: - Added `draw_multiline_string` function. - Added additional parameters to all draw functions. - New font fallback API similar to `DynamicFont` fallback (single list of `FontData`).
Major Font API changes: Old: ```c++ Size2 get_string_size(const String &p_string) const; void draw(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, const String &p_text, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_clip_w = -1, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1)) const; void draw_halign(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, HAlign p_align, float p_width, const String &p_text, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1)) const; Size2 get_wordwrap_string_size(const String &p_string, float p_width) const; Size2 get_char_size(char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0) const; float draw_char(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), bool p_outline = false) const; ``` New: ```c++ Size2 get_string_size(const String &p_text, int p_size = -1) const; void draw_string(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, const String &p_text, HAlign p_align = HALIGN_LEFT, float p_width = -1, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0), uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_KASHIDA | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_WORD_BOUND) const; Size2 get_multiline_string_size(const String &p_text, float p_width = -1, int p_size = -1, uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::BREAK_MANDATORY | TextServer::BREAK_WORD_BOUND) const; void draw_multiline_string(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, const String &p_text, HAlign p_align = HALIGN_LEFT, float p_width = -1, int p_max_lines = -1, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0), uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::BREAK_MANDATORY | TextServer::BREAK_WORD_BOUND | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_KASHIDA | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_WORD_BOUND) const; Size2 get_char_size(char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0, int p_size = -1) const; float draw_char(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0)) const; ```
#### TextServer interface structure: ![ts_map](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/92443294-fb904000-f1b9-11ea-806a-0dcc61b17cda.png) #### Test projects: GDNative plugin template: https://github.com/bruvzg/gdnative_text_server_template #### Current status: - Backend: Working. - Controls: All controls except `RichTextLabel` and containers support mirroring and use `TexeServer` base text rendering. ### Input: Input of the characters outside BMP (codes `> 0xFFFF`, emoji, rare/ancient scripts, e.t.c.) is fully tested on macOS, Windows 10, Android and Wine under macOS. Should work on Linux (input is received as UTF-8 string), but might need some more testing with different input methods. On iOS, it should work as well (input is received as UTF-16 string), but I can't test it since I do not have any iOS device, and simulator currently do not have all Metal features supported to run Godot.

Everything seems to be working now (except for the RichTextLabel, which will be done as separate PR), but probably I have missed some glitches.

List of changes in the PR:
- Added `TextServerManager` (control loading, enumeration and switching for `TextServer`s).
- Added `TextServer` interface (handles fonts, text rendering and line breaking and input related stuff).
  - Handles:
    - BiDi and Text shaping.
    - Inline object/image embedding to the text flow.
    - Line/word breaking.
    - Fitting text to width and aligning to tab stops.
    - Input carets, selections and hit testing.
  - Implementations:
    - `TextServerFallback` module (simple text server without BiDi and shaping support).
    - `TextServerAdvanced` module (ICU/HarfBuzz/Graphite based text server), note: after `godot-cpp` catch up with the master, it can be converted to GDNative library with minimal changes (changing header names, build config, and adding wrapper from the demo repository - https://github.com/bruvzg/gdnative_text_server_template) and we'll need something like https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/831 to used it as library with the editor and project manager.
      - ICU optional dictionary data (cut down to 4 MB) can be embedded into the executable (default for `tools` build) or loaded for PCK (default for templates).
    - GDNative interface for text servers.
- `Font`
  - Font management moved to the `TextServer` to better handle shaping and font substitution.
  - `BitmapFont` and `DynamicFont` replaced with generic `Font`+`FontData`
  - Text can be drawn using LRU cached `font->draw_string`/`font->get_string_size` calls or by using `TextLine` / `TextParagraph` objects.
- Font size and outline color/size moved from base font to separate theme and draw functions options.
- Added interface mirroring for:
  - Child order in the containers.
  - Internal elements of complex controls (tree, itemlist, etc)
  - Added some mirrored icons and styles.
  - Interface mirroring can be overridden for each control, inherited or determined based on locale.
- Modified Windows and macOS input to handle UTF-16 input (multiple codepoints for one character).
- All controls modified to use new text rendering, line/word breaking and have additional properties added to control font features and text layout.
- BiDi override for handling specially structured text (URIs, paths, source code) added to `TextEdit`, `Label` and `LineEdit` (with optional used defined callback support for custom overrides).
- Added editor plugins for:
  - Font substitution control.
  - ICU data export.

Note: There are still places where BiDi override (path not displayed correctly in RTL layout) need to be applied, but some of them are `RichTextLabel`s, I'll runt through all UI and add them after finishing with `RichTextLabel`.

## Changes to the Node API: ### `Control` changes: --- 1. Layout mirroring control (in `Control` and `Window`): `is_layout_rtl()`, `layout_direction` property and `NOTIFICATION_LAYOUT_DIRECTION_CHANGED` Layout mirrors the order of the controls in the container and internal components of the control, margins and anchors. (top to bottom: LTR, RTL) (layout swap RTL↔LTR) ![ly](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/95650507-c2b2f600-0aec-11eb-92c4-868446236ef6.gif) For the testing purpose, layout can be force to `RTL` be setting `display/window/force_right_to_left_layout_direction` project setting. `layout_direction` values: - `LAYOUT_DIRECTION_INHERITED` - use layout direction of the parent control, or locale for root control (default). - `LAYOUT_DIRECTION_LOCALE` - use locale to determine direction, to work with editor `Translation::get_tool_locale()` function is added (identical to `get_loacle()` for running projects). - `TEXT_DIRECTION_LTR` and `TEXT_DIRECTION_RTL` - force specific direction, useful if you need fixed layout (e.g. buttons with directional arrows). --- 2. Text layout control (only for controls with text, or their elements, e.g. TreeItem ): `text_direction` property - controls base direction (default direction for not strongly directional text). - `TEXT_DIRECTION_INHERITED` - use the same direction as layout direction (default). - `TEXT_DIRECTION_AUTO` - use locale and text content (first strongly directional character) to determine direction. - `TEXT_DIRECTION_LTR` and `TEXT_DIRECTION_RTL` - force specific default direction. (Base direction can affect order of the elements in the mixed text: top-to-bottom Auto, LTR, RTL). In most cases base direction should be the same as the language of text (default behavior). --- `structured_text_bidi_override` property and `_structured_text_parser` callback (only for controls with text): BiDi algorithm is designed for natural text and in can't correctly display strings with a special structure (e.g URI, file path, regular expressions or source code): ![Screenshot 2020-10-05 at 09 06 27](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/95046822-9c0c4e00-06ed-11eb-93ce-fdbb3cdd9874.png) For example path for this directory structure will be displayed incorrectly (top string), structured text override add a callback function to split text into segments, then BiDi is applied to each of them individually (bottom string). --- `language` property (only for controls with text): Overrides locale for the control, and also controls language specific line breaking rules and shaping: --- `ot_features` property (only for controls with text): Controls OpenType font features for the control: e.g. ligature types to use, number styles, small caps etc. (list of tags: https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/typography/opentype/spec/featuretags) --- `Control` and `Window` functions `add_theme_font_size_override`, `get_theme_font_size`, `has_theme_font_size`, `has_theme_font_size_override` and `Theme` functions: `clear_font_size`, `get_font_size`, `get_font_size_list`, `has_font_size`, `set_font_size` Control font size in the similar manner to existing function for the `Font`, value `-1` is used as unset/default (same as `null` for the font). --- `Label`: `outline_size` and `shadow_outline_size` - used to set outline size for the label. --- `LineEdit` and `TextEdit`: `caret_mid_grapheme` disabled by default. If enabled caret can be moved to each individual component of grapheme (e.g. diacritics and base character), if not moves over the whole grapheme. (e.g in this case pressing delete will only remove diacritic, but pressing ← will jump over the full combined character) ![Screenshot 2020-10-05 at 07 59 06](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/95047800-66686480-06ef-11eb-9b4a-24c461042e75.png) (with mid caret enabled ← will jump to the position in between diacritic and the base character, caret will be displayed in the middle of combined character). ![Screenshot 2020-10-05 at 07 59 44](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/7645683/95048028-c52dde00-06ef-11eb-983e-873f23db8d71.png) I have encountered apps using both, but default behavior seems to be most common, not sure mid caret mode is useful at all. --- `LineEdit` and `TextEdit`: `display_control` - if enabled control characters will be visible in the text (as special symbols if available in the font or hex codes if not), useful for more complex BiDi layout control. Also, popup menu to insert some of them as well as joiner characters to control line breaking added to the `LineEdit` and `TextEdit`.

## `Font` and `FontData`:

Actual font implementation is move to text server, `Font` and `FontData` classes are used for easy access to TS font API.

### `FontData`:

Single font file (or memory buffer), handles both dynamic and bitmap fonts:

Additional language and script overrides can be set for each font data, these are used for font substitution in following cases:
- for the languages that are using the same script but different style: e.g. different Arabic languages use Naskh and Nastaliq styles and different fonts but it's the same script (writing system), used by editor to handle Urdu and Persian locales.
- script overrides can be useful for, rare languages and big font sets to select proper font faster (TrueType fonts have flags only for some scripts, if not selected manually shaped will try every font in the list instead of going directly to the correct one).
- script overrides can be used for the fonts with incomplete character sets, e.g many Latin fonts have limited set of Greek characters for scientific text, that is not enough for real Greek text, but such font will have flag for Greek support. In this case you may want to add override to avoid using it for Greek and add separate font.

Note: Shaped will try all fonts until all character are found, overrides only affect search order.

Note: there was `distance_field_hint` property in the BitmapFont that seems to be not implemented, I have preserved it as is in new `FontData` as is.

`FontData` have `base_size` used to load on font creation and which is used for draw function with `p_size == -1`, but it is capable to load and use any font size on demand.

### `Font`:
Font "fallback"/substitution uses single list of the `FontData` in the similar manner `DynamicFont` was, but there's no primary one since order is determined by language/script support and overrides.

`draw/draw_haling` Function merged to the single one, and multiline draw function was added, each of of this have `size` function with the same API and use LRU cache to reuse shaped data.

Additionally, `core/math/math_defs.h:: HALIGN_FILL` is added for use of haligned draw.

`CanvasItem` text draw functions are changed in the same way.

If font size is set to `-1`, base_size is used.

```
	Size2 get_string_size(const String &p_text, int p_size = -1) const;
	Size2 get_multiline_string_size(const String &p_text, float p_width = -1, int p_size = -1, uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::BREAK_MANDATORY | TextServer::BREAK_WORD_BOUND) const;

	void draw_string(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, const String &p_text, HAlign p_align = HALIGN_LEFT, float p_width = -1, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0), uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_KASHIDA | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_WORD_BOUND) const;
	void draw_multiline_string(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, const String &p_text, HAlign p_align = HALIGN_LEFT, float p_width = -1, int p_max_lines = -1, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0), uint8_t p_flags = TextServer::BREAK_MANDATORY | TextServer::BREAK_WORD_BOUND | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_KASHIDA | TextServer::JUSTIFICATION_WORD_BOUND) const;
```

Char draw functions are preserved (for drawing single chars, numbers and other simple stuff), these functions do not use `TextServer` shaping or BiDi and draw chars directly:
```
	Size2 get_char_size(char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0, int p_size = -1) const;
	float draw_char(RID p_canvas_item, const Point2 &p_pos, char32_t p_char, char32_t p_next = 0, int p_size = -1, const Color &p_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1), int p_outline_size = 0, const Color &p_outline_modulate = Color(1, 1, 1, 0)) const;
```

Note: font functions like `get_ascent/get_descent` return average of the `FontData` ascents/descents, in the real text, character elements can be outside of font ascent and descent and these functions are only useful as rough estimate (e.g. for empty text field size).

For the static texts, local (control specific) cache, and more precise control `TextLine` and `TextPragraph` classes are added as the easy-to-use wrapper over TS API.

> Layout mirrors the order of the controls in the container and internal components of the control, manually places controls are not moved, but additional layout dependent anchor presets are added PRESET_xxx_BEGIN/PRESET_xxx_END in addition to PRESET_xxx_LEFT/PRESET_xxx_RIGHT:

I am not really sure this is the best implementation. Those are presets used by the `set_anchors_and_margins` presets, which is basically a helper to call several `set_anchor` and `set_margin`. As this one is a helper, it kind of annoys me to allow RTL feature only in the preset setting function, but not in the normal calls to `set_anchor` and `set_margin`.

I would eventually suggest to instead add an argument to all those function, to switch a to a RTL layout. So for `set_margin`, `set_margins_preset`, `set_anchor`, `set_anchors_preset`, `set_anchor_and_margin` and `set_anchors_and_margins_preset` I would add an argument to switch to the opposite layout. We could also rename (or create an alias for compatibility reasons) the MARGIN_LEFT and MARGIN_RIGHT constants to MARGIN_HBEGIN and MARGIN_HEND (or somehow like that).

## `TextServer` API: TextServer provides the following APIs: `font` functions for Font creation and control, a backend for `FontData`. `shaped_text` functions for text buffers, a backend for `Font` draw/size functions and `TextLine`, `TextPragraph`: Shaped text buffer APIs are lazy and won't do any processing until output data is requested, substring will reuse shaping results of the parent string until they are changed. ``` bool shaped_text_add_string(RID p_shaped, const String &p_text, const Vector &p_fonts, int p_size, const String &p_ot_features = "", const String &p_language = ""); bool shaped_text_add_object(RID p_shaped, Variant p_key, const Size2 &p_size, VAlign p_inline_align = VALIGN_CENTER); ``` Functions are used to fill up the buffer with segments of text and inlined objects (e.g. images and tables in RichTextLabel, object placement are affected by BiDi and sizes used during line breaking). Text server provides functions for breaking text into lines and words (can use optionally use ICU data dictionaries for better breaking) and extraction of substrings (without reshaping). Also, it has helper functions for input controls: - caret handling: when caret is in between the text segments with different directionally, it can be displayed in multiple locations in the same time (input will appear in the different places of text depending on the inputted text direction). As well as caret movement over grapheme (see. mid gr. caret above.) - getting selection rectangles, since selection in the bidirectional text is not always continues and characters can overlap, it's easier to get it in one go. - hit testing for caret placement. --- Text buffer workflow looks as following: 1. Buffer is filled with text spans and objects (for the rest of processing it's just single "Object replacement character" with the specified size) and its properties are set. (at this stage no processing is done, input data is stored as is). 2. As soon as any output is requested (e.g. get_size, draw, or get_glyphs is called). - Text is split to the segments (runs) based on the script used (custom iterator based on ICU Unicode data functions). - ICU BiDi is used to detect directions and order of the text segments (in case structured text override is active it's used multiple times), BiDi context is saved to be reused with substrings. - Each segment of the text with the uniform script, direction, language and font (language and font are taken from the spans) is shaped (characters are transformed to the font specific glyphs and offset of the glyphs are determined) using HarfBuzz, in the order returned by BiDi. FontData order is determined based on script and language, shaper will try to use each one until all subruns are shaped successfully or there are no more fonts in the list. Failed characters are stored as is and later displayed as the hexcodes when string is drawn. As the result all glyphs are stored to the vector in the order in which they are displayed. 3. As soon as any of the line breaking functions is called. - ICU break iterator is used to determine line and word breaks, in case there's no space character between the words, virtual zero width glyph is added, flags for breaks are added to existing glyphs. - Glyphs are sorted in the logical order (as their source characters were in the original string). - Sorted glyph widths and flags are used to determine line breaks. 4. As soon as fit to wight is called: - Word breaking is done if it was not called by line breaking. - Kashidas are detected in word, or added to the word in appropriate places. - First kashidas and then spaces are extended to fit the text. (top-to-bottom: kashida and space justification, no justification, space justification) Breaks and kashidas are reused for the substring alignment without repeating the step.

> I would eventually suggest to instead add an argument to all those function, to switch a to a RTL layout. 

This might be better solution indeed.

What's the reason for not translating editor/project settings and property names?

> What's the reason for not translating editor/project settings and property names?

Mostly that those settings are generated directly from their identifier (`some_section/some_setting` becomes "Some Section / Some Settings"), and if we translate them we introduce some additional friction:
- The visual setting name will no longer match the identifier.
- It will also not match what is being described in the class reference.
- When you add new settings yourself in Project Settings, you'd need to be able to provide both an identifier that can match existing categories if you wish so, and a translation for the sections and name substrings.

Initially it was considered simpler to just keep it automated and thus in English. We could reconsider this if we find ways to alleviate the issues, but it would require a significant rethinking of the UI to accommodate it without losing the flexibility of the current automated system.

issue_context.title: CJK glyph flow in UI labels should not line break on whitespace
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
3.2.2 Stable


**OS/device including version:**
Windows 10 64-bit


**Issue description:**
When rendering east-Asian language text inside a label, the node is treating whitespace codepoints as a line break point, even though it may be inappropriate. The result is essentially showing one sentence per line, if spaces are used to separate sentences. A semi-correct behavior can be attained by _not_ placing whitespace between sentences.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/141511/88446178-672a7380-cded-11ea-8f37-12ef4c3ac9b2.png)

(The text featured is translated with Google Translate; I apologize if it doesn't make any sense to Japanese readers)

[Wikipedia has an article on line-breaking for East-Asian Languages.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_breaking_rules_in_East_Asian_languages) I believe this is a fairly important feature for supporting these locales as this also impacts presentation of labels in the Godot Editor, which would result in a subpar editor experience.


**Steps to reproduce:**
1. Create a Label node
2. Set its text to a combination of English and Japanese sentences.


**Minimal reproduction project:**
[CJKWordWrapIssue.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/4974751/CJKWordWrapIssue.zip)

This zip contains `NotoSans-Regular.otf` and `NotoSansJP-Regular.ttf`, both of which are used and distributed under the terms of the SIL Open Font License.
comments:
As far as I know, breaking after arbitrary CJK glyph is not correct either, reliable detection of words in CJK, Thai and any other languages when using hyphenation will require use of dictionary. Also, many languages use alternative space marks.

See [UAX #29, Unicode Text Segmentation](https://unicode.org/reports/tr29/) and [UAX #14, Unicode Line Breaking Algorithm ](https://unicode.org/reports/tr14/) for more information.

As soon as [complex text layouts](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-proposals/issues/1180) are implemented, correct line / word breaking will be handled by use of [ICU BreakIterator](http://userguide.icu-project.org/boundaryanalysis).
